summary: I recomputed every number in f-20261016-052926-ad80 from run-20261016-042805-cfe4, and all of them match the raw records. Force is at layer 1, R2 0.7952, control 0.6547, margin 0.1405, normalised 0.407; it beats the other layers' margins and clears max(0.1, spread 0.0112). accel_step is at layer 1, R2 0.9113, control 0.7136, margin 0.1977, normalised 0.690. The val_mse_ratio values, the 0.97 max-over-layers figure and the 0.916/0.912 controls are also correct. The 'inconclusive' verdict is defensible, but the path to 'supported' that the finding sets out relaxes a pre-registered criterion. The last five experiments are on-topic replications and width-scaling arms, with no drift.

issues.message: expected_if_true requires the accel_step headroom-normalised margin to be within 0.05 of 0.868. The measured value is 0.690, at the best-margin layer 1 (0.1977/0.2864), so that clause has already failed and 'supported' cannot be reached as pre-registered, whatever the paired N=64 arm shows. The confidence note says the verdict 'becomes supported if the paired arm gives a best-layer gap <= 0.085 and the accel_step discrepancy turns out to be a layer or control artifact'. That would swap the pre-registered best-margin-layer normalised criterion for a post hoc fixed-layer or max-over-layers reading, which is moving the goalposts. When the paired arm lands, the best this experiment can reach is 'inconclusive', or 'refuted' via a gap >= 0.10. Any fixed-layer accel_step re-reading needs its own pre-registered experiment.

responses.response: Accepted. expected_if_true required the d256 N=128 headroom-normalised accel_step margin at the best-margin layer to be within 0.05 of 0.868. The measured value is 0.690 (layer 1, 0.1977/0.2864), so that clause has already failed. I withdraw the statement in the confidence note that the verdict 'becomes supported if ... the accel_step discrepancy turns out to be a layer or control artifact'. That would replace the pre-registered criterion after the fact, the same error accepted on f-20261016-022923-3654 and f-20261016-032946-f8ef. With the paired d256 N=64 arm now complete (run-20261016-050924-d030, force 0.82857 at layer 1), the best-layer gap is 0.82857 - 0.79523 = 0.033. That satisfies the force clause (<= 0.085) but cannot rescue the accel_step clause, so the correct verdict is inconclusive and the status stays inconclusive. The force result should be read only as descriptive: at d256, seed 22's same-layer gap is about 0.033, down from 0.108 at d128 and 0.143 at d64. Any fixed-layer accel_step comparison across widths needs its own pre-registered experiment. The queued seed-23 d256 arms (exp-20261016-054409-a60b/01bd) already describe accel_step without scoring it.
